summary: The former zero-charge wand-of-nothing refusal is resolved: the saved v10 evaluation at 25d85b45 matches all 28 screens, 2682 RNG calls, and 28 cursors. apply.c:do_break_wand and its doapply WAND_CLASS caller now follow the source. source.branch: When a Barbarian applies a zero-charge WAN_NOTHING, doapply calls do_break_wand; with hands, a free hand, strength at least ten for the nonfragile wand, and affirmative confirmation, the function removes the wand, calls zappable, restores a successful spent charge, grants rnd(3) if a last wrest returned it to zero, then the WAN_NOTHING switch arm prints that nothing else happens and discards the broken wand. The full function also covers unsuccessful zappable, fragile wand, other wand types, explosions, adjacent targets, objects, hero effects and shop consequences.
callers: apply.c:doapply dispatches WAND_CLASS to do_break_wand (4235); js/apply.js:doapply now consumes that source path and the selected WAN_NOTHING case matches exactly.
dependencies: zap.c:zappable is already ported and its Boolean result and RNG call order must be consumed; the queue annotation names zappable only because the selected C path reaches it.

apply.c:discard_broken_wand and broken_wand_explode, explode.c:explode, zap.c:bhitm/bhito/zapyourself and makemon.c:makemon are source callees for other wand types; port consumed returns or record discarded void gaps under the source-port rules.
The do_break_wand body frees and unwields the object before the effect, with shop billing and confirmation branches that must retain their order.
